lesson_title: The Notebook or the Count: Inventory Systems
hook_text: A case of cooldrink walks out the back door. One shop notices. The other calls it a sale.
clip_script: Two spaza owners, same street, two ways of running stock. The first keeps a notebook: every time a loaf goes out, she writes down not just the R18 she took, but that a loaf costing R13 left the shelf. Any hour of any day, she knows what should be on her shelves. The second keeps no notebook — he records what he buys, takes the money at the till, and at year end he closes up, counts everything left, and does one sum: what I started with, plus what I bought, minus what's still here — that must be what I sold. Both reach a number. But watch what the second owner just gave up. If a case of cooldrink walked out the back door in June, his sum quietly calls it SOLD — because there's nothing left to count and nothing to compare against. Her notebook would have said: R2 400 should be here. His system says: business was just a bit disappointing this year.
visual_style: Two spaza counters side by side; one with a glowing running tally above the shelves, the other dark until a year-end torch sweep counts the shelves; a case of cooldrink slipping out a back door and being absorbed silently into one owner's cost-of-sales bar.
mood: Quietly revealing — a small story with a sharp control lesson.
pacing: Parallel-story rhythm, one beat per system, hard landing on the stolen case.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the year-end sum yourself.
